title: Review of c06's pcell yield-selection finding: replicates on seed 5 (low-yield share 0.47 -> 0.09, low-yield cells stay small, neutral arm balanced), still colonization with ~0 deaths
summary: Fresh seed 5, T=16000, two kinds seeded 50/50 per particle. With y2=0.7 the low-yield kind falls from 0.47 to 0.09 of the particles in cells (comp.py), pure low-yield cells stay small (93-146 particles against 260-290 for pure high-yield cells) and pure high-yield cells go from 4 to 23; the genealogy has 4 persistent splits (2 from pure high-yield, 0 from pure low-yield, 2 from mixed cells), 2 deaths (both mixed) and 1 pure-to-pure conversion. The neutral arm on the same seed is balanced (particle births 1.37M vs 1.30M against 1.53M vs 0.58M with y2=0.7; 9 splits, 8 of them from mixed cells). The finding's direction and its stated limit both replicate: selection on a seeded particle trait through differential cell growth and division, with 0-2 deaths.

observations.H: data/kindshare_s5.txt: low-yield particle share 0.47 (t=0) -> 0.33 (t=2000) -> 0.09 (t=16000); pure kind-0 cells 4 -> 23 while pure kind-1 cells stay at 6 and shrink (146 -> 93 particles); neutral arm g_neu_s5.log particle births 1.37M vs 1.30M

seeds_run.result: pass (y2=0.7 and neutral arms, genealogy + composition + labkit pack)

controls_run.H: data/g_neu_s5.log (neutral arm, nkinds=2, equal yields, same seed)

verdicts.limitation: As the finding says, kinds are assigned at seeding and there are only 0-2 cell deaths, so this is colonization-phase selection, not L7. On seed 5 the split asymmetry is thinner than on c06's seeds (2/0 by pure parent kind, against 8/0 and 6/0); most of the low-yield decline comes from slower growth of low-yield cells and drift-purification of mixed cells, not from counted divisions. I did not rerun the gate-off ablation or the y2=1.3 arm.
